android-settings.add.added.one: 1 person joins on first sign-in to {app}.
android-settings.add.added.other: {n} people join on first sign-in to {app}.

android-settings.add.note: Added to “{name}” directly, without needing to accept. People who've used {app} join immediately; others join when they first sign in with this email.
android-settings.add.title: Add members
android-settings.appearance.title: Appearance
android-settings.changelog.title: Changelog
android-settings.connect.deleteText: Disconnects from Slack. You need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

android-settings.connect.deleteTextSessi.one: Disconnects from Slack. Its chat is kept but gets no new messages. Delete the app in Slack yourself.
android-settings.connect.deleteTextSessi.other: Disconnects from Slack. Its {n} chats are kept but get no new messages. Delete the app in Slack yourself.

android-settings.connect.everyMessage: Gets every message it can see.
android-settings.connect.noSession: No chat yet; the next message starts one.
android-settings.connect.noSessions: No chats yet. @{name} in Slack to start one.
android-settings.connect.ownerNote: The owner sees this connect under “Mine”.
android-settings.connect.runtime: Runs on {runtime}, which can't be changed; for another runtime, add a new connect. Ongoing chats keep their settings.
android-settings.connect.slackAppNote: Changes go straight to the Slack app
android-settings.connects.note: A connect is how people reach {app}, such as a Slack app. Each connect runs on one station and is bound to one model.
android-settings.connects.title: Connects
android-settings.agentEnv.note: Agents, logins and tasks started by this station load these variables, commonly to set an HTTP proxy. One NAME=value per line; you can paste a .env file. Leave a masked value as it is to keep it. A Profile's variable of the same name takes precedence. After saving, idle agent processes restart; running ones pick up the change after their current turn.
android-settings.agentEnv.title: Agent environment variables
android-settings.env.note: The runtime starts with these variables to reach your model service. {route} in a value is replaced with the chat's route ID.
android-settings.env.title: Environment variables
android-settings.files.clearAll.text: Deletes {size} of chat history and files stored on this phone. They download again when opened.
android-settings.files.clearAll.title: Clear all?
android-settings.files.clearChat.text: Deletes {size} stored on this phone. It downloads again when opened.
android-settings.files.data.text: Sign-in, chat lists, settings and more; can't be deleted
android-settings.files.drive.sub: Up to 2 GB; least recently opened files are deleted first
android-settings.files.drive.text: Deletes text, images, videos and other files opened from station files. They download again when opened.
android-settings.files.fill.max.sub: Larger files aren't finished in the background
android-settings.files.fill.on.sub: Opened files finish in the background
android-settings.files.fill.title: Background downloads
android-settings.files.messages.clear: Deletes this chat's messages stored on this phone. They load again from the station when the chat is opened.
android-settings.files.messages.text: Reloaded from the station when opened
android-settings.files.note: Chat history and files opened on this phone are cached here, so they open again without downloading. Deleting them only affects this phone, not the station.
android-settings.files.temporary.text: Deletes temporary files left by image markup and similar tasks.
android-settings.files.title: Local cache
android-settings.files.web.text: Deletes content cached from previewed pages. They load again when opened.
android-settings.flow.appToken: On the Socket Mode page, generate an App-Level Token and copy it (starts with xapp-; scopes preset).
android-settings.flow.installManual: App created. Install it to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) from the OAuth page.
android-settings.flow.installOauth: App created. Install it to the workspace: tap “Allow” in Slack and the bot token goes to the station.
android-settings.flow.manual: Set up manually, no config token
android-settings.flow.manual1: Create a Slack app from {app}'s manifest.
android-settings.flow.manual2: On its Socket Mode page, generate an App-Level Token (scopes preset).
android-settings.flow.manual3: On the Install App page, install to the workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token.
android-settings.flow.manualInSlack: Set up in Slack manually, no config token
android-settings.flow.noModels: No models enabled in this station's profiles. Enable some under Profile on the station page.
android-settings.flow.noProfileNote: Connects run models through a profile. Add one first.
android-settings.flow.permsNote: Permissions default to all on; change them later under the connect's “Slack app”.
android-settings.flow.removeTokenText: {app} stops using it to build and edit apps in this Slack workspace. Existing apps and connects aren't affected; you can add it again later.
android-settings.flow.title: Add connect
android-settings.flow.tokenNote: With a Slack config token, {app} creates the app for you: set its name, icon and permissions here instead of in Slack's admin pages. Only you can use the token.
android-settings.flow.whichTeam: Choose the Slack workspace whose config token creates the app
android-settings.login.codexNote: On the OpenAI page that opens, sign in with the ChatGPT account {app} should use, then paste the code. This screen continues automatically when done. If the page says device code sign-in is off, turn it on in ChatGPT's security settings first.
android-settings.login.opencodeNote: On the OpenCode page that opens, sign in, check that its code matches this one, then choose the workspace with Go and authorize. This page continues by itself once you are done.
android-settings.login.kimiNote: On the Kimi page that opens, sign in with the account that has Kimi Code, check that the code matches, then authorize. This page continues by itself once you are done.
android-settings.login.grokNote: On the xAI page that opens, sign in with the account that has SuperGrok or X Premium+, enter the code, then approve. This page continues by itself once you are done.
android-settings.login.cursorNote: On the Cursor page that opens, sign in and confirm. This page continues by itself once you are done.
android-settings.login.copyOpen: Copy code and open sign-in page
android-settings.login.note: Sign-in happens on the machine running {app}; you only need to authorize it in the browser.
android-settings.login.openPageRest: , sign in with the Claude account {app} should use, and agree.
android-settings.login.step1Short: On the page, sign in with the Claude account {app} should use and agree
android-settings.login.step1ShortDevin: On the page, sign in with the Devin account {app} should use
android-settings.login.step2Short: Paste the code the page shows here
android-settings.machine.added: Profile added with this machine's login
android-settings.machine.title: Already signed in here
android-settings.me.deleteText: The account {email} will be deleted. Workspaces that are only yours are deleted with it, and their stations leave them; the other workspaces you're in remove you. Chats and files on your stations are on your own machines and stay untouched. This can't be undone.
android-settings.me.title: Account
android-settings.members.moveOutText: They lose access to this workspace's stations. You can invite them again later.
android-settings.members.title: Members
android-settings.mode.back: Switching back to single chat later resumes the original one.
android-settings.mode.keepSession: Resumes the single chat it was bound to before.
android-settings.mode.mention: From then on, only @-mentioned threads go into chats; replies in threads already in a chat still arrive.
android-settings.mode.mentionOff: Gets every message it can see in its channels.
android-settings.mode.mentionOn: Replies in an @-mentioned thread don't need another @.
android-settings.mode.newSession: The next message starts a new single chat, or pick an existing chat after switching.
android-settings.mode.noMention: No @ needed: every message in every channel and DM it can see goes to the agent. Usage rises noticeably.
android-settings.mode.oldThreads: Threads from the single chat need a new @ to continue, which opens a new chat without the earlier context.

android-settings.mode.running.one: 1 chat is running; it finishes its current turn.
android-settings.mode.running.other: {n} chats are running; they finish their current turn.

android-settings.mode.title: Chat mode
android-settings.mode.toMulti: The bound chat gets no new messages. Each thread then opens its own chat when @-mentioned.
android-settings.mode.toSingle: All its messages then go into one chat. Existing per-thread chats get no new messages, even replies in their threads. Their history is kept.
android-settings.models.empty: Once the profile is checked, its models are listed here. Tick the ones to use.
android-settings.models.note: Only ticked models can be chosen for new chats and connects.
android-settings.notify.title: Notifications
android-settings.telemetry.title: Send usage statistics and error reports
android-settings.profile.background: Move running commands to the background when a message arrives
android-settings.profile.backgroundOff: New messages wait until the running command or subagent finishes
android-settings.profile.backgroundOn: Commands and subagents continue in the background; the agent reads the message immediately.
android-settings.profile.deleteText: Removes it from {app} only; its config directory and login stay. Sessions running on it move to another Profile, or stop when there is none.
android-settings.profile.disableText: {app} stops using the {runtime} login on this machine. The login itself stays, and you can use it again later. Sessions running on it move to another Profile, or stop when there is none.
android-settings.profile.fastNote: For chats on Plan default; Fast uses more allowance or credits
android-settings.profile.machineNote: To switch accounts, sign in again or sign out, use {runtime} on this machine; this profile follows. To stop using it, turn it off (top-right menu).
android-settings.profile.noUsers: No connects use this profile yet
android-settings.profile.offline: {name} is offline; available once it reconnects
android-settings.profile.subscriptionNot: Sign-in happens on the machine running {app}; you only need to authorize it in the browser. The profile is added once sign-in succeeds.
android-settings.profiles.note: Accounts agents use to run models. Ones that need attention come first; open one to see why and how to fix it.
android-settings.quota.title: Allowance
android-settings.relays.hint: An iroh-relay https address. The web app requires a publicly issued certificate (such as Let's Encrypt); self-signed certificates aren't supported.
android-settings.relays.lead: Besides {app}'s relays, stations and members' devices also connect through these, automatically using the fastest.
android-settings.relays.title: Relays
android-settings.ways.directNote: Straight through both routers, no relay
android-settings.ways.lead: Members' devices reach this workspace's stations only in the ways turned on. Keep at least one relay on.
android-settings.ways.title: Connections
android-settings.run.noModels: No models enabled in {runtime} profiles. Enable some under Profile on the station page.
android-settings.run.note: New chats use the new settings; ongoing ones keep theirs.
android-settings.run.title: Model
android-settings.session.note: Messages to “{name}” now go into the chosen chat. The previous chat is kept but gets no new messages from this connect.
android-settings.session.title: Choose chat
android-settings.signIn.many: Sign in with several accounts and switch workspaces any time.
android-settings.signIn.note: After sign-in, every station and chat in your workspaces shows up here.
android-settings.signIn.title: Keep your agents working
android-settings.slack.accessToken: That's the Access Token. Use the Refresh Token below it (xoxe-1-…).
android-settings.slack.approveNote: Permissions changed; approve them in Slack to take effect.
android-settings.slack.group.base.note: Get messages when @-mentioned; read and reply in its channels, DMs and group DMs. Required.
android-settings.slack.group.canvases.no: Create, edit and read canvases, e.g. write a plan or report as a canvas in a channel.
android-settings.slack.group.channels.no: Create channels, invite people, see joins and new channels.
android-settings.slack.group.connect.not: See, send and accept invites to channels shared with other companies.
android-settings.slack.group.customize.n: Change display name and icon per message.
android-settings.slack.group.dm.note: Open DMs with one or more people
android-settings.slack.group.extras.note: Unfurl links, set reminders, read DND and call status
android-settings.slack.group.files.note: Read attachments; upload screenshots, logs and other files.
android-settings.slack.group.lists.note: Create, edit and read Slack Lists, e.g. keep a task list.
android-settings.slack.group.more.note: Set its presence, read message metadata and workspace settings, embed video links, answer slash commands.
android-settings.slack.group.people.note: Read emails, profiles, user groups, workspace info and custom emoji
android-settings.slack.group.public.note: Reply in public channels without an invite
android-settings.slack.group.reactions.n: Mark progress with emoji, pin messages, manage bookmarks
android-settings.slack.group.search.note: Search public messages and files, find people by name, look up context to answer.
android-settings.slack.group.topics.note: Set topics and purposes of channels and DMs; invite people to channels.
Create user groups, edit members, start and update calls.
android-settings.slack.iconNote: Pick one below, or upload an image.
android-settings.slack.name: Name
android-settings.slack.needToken: To edit the app here, add your app config token for this Slack workspace. Only you can use it; others on this station can't see it.
android-settings.slack.noApp: Can't find this connect's Slack app ({error}). Switch to a valid token and try again.
android-settings.slack.notConnected: Edit its app here once it's connected to Slack.
android-settings.slack.refreshToken: The Refresh Token starts with xoxe-1-.
android-settings.slack.step1: Open api.slack.com/apps and sign in to the Slack workspace the bot will join.
android-settings.slack.step2: Scroll to “Your App Configuration Tokens” at the bottom, tap Generate Token and pick this workspace.
android-settings.slack.step3: Paste the Refresh Token (xoxe-1-…) below. {app} renews it automatically from then on.
android-settings.slack.updatedApprove: Updated; approve the new permissions in Slack
android-settings.station.addNote: A station is a machine running {app}. Name it, then run the generated command in its terminal: it installs {app} and joins.
android-settings.station.addHere: Or add this Mac itself: the station is downloaded here and joins this workspace, with no command to run.
android-settings.station.addHerePc: Or add this PC itself: the station is downloaded here and joins this workspace, with no command to run.
android-settings.station.firstNote: Agents work on your machines. Start by adding a Mac or Linux machine.
android-settings.station.joined: “{name}” joined. You can open it now.
android-settings.station.name: Name
android-settings.station.removeText: It disconnects from {app} cloud and members can't reach it from here. {app} and data on the machine stay; you can add it again later.
android-settings.station.imageFailed: Couldn't read this image or make it small enough
android-settings.station.runNote: Works on macOS (Apple silicon), Linux and WSL on Windows, including machines with {app} already. It installs {app}, joins this workspace and keeps running in the background. Then add profiles on its station page.
android-settings.station.wait: No stations yet. An admin needs to add one.
android-settings.station.waiting: Waiting for the machine to join… Continues automatically once the command runs · Command valid for 1 hour
android-settings.stations.offline: Offline: open {app} on this machine to reconnect
android-settings.title: Settings
android-settings.tokens.note: Change one or both; a blank one keeps the saved value.
android-settings.waiting.removeText: Removes it from {app} only; the app stays in Slack. Delete it from the app's settings in Slack if you no longer need it.
android-settings.workspace.title: Workspace

android-settings.workspace.deleteText.one: All members lose access, and 1 station disconnects from {app} cloud (data on the station stays).
android-settings.workspace.deleteText.other: All members lose access, and {n} stations disconnect from {app} cloud (data on them stays).

android-settings.workspace.leaveText: You'll lose access to its stations and need a new invite to return.
android-settings.workspace.name: Workspace name
android-settings.vault.title: Secrets
android-settings.vault.readOnly: The web shows names only: open and approve in the app
android-settings.vault.needsLockWhy: Secrets only go to devices confirmed in security mode
android-settings.vault.notSigner: This device isn't confirmed in security mode yet
android-settings.vault.notSignerWhy: Confirm it to use secrets on this device
android-settings.vault.offWhat: Keep tokens, API keys and SSH keys here: the values only ever exist in your app
android-settings.vault.offAgents: Agents ask to use one, and you approve it on your phone
android-settings.vault.offUnlock: Opening and approving take your fingerprint or screen lock
android-settings.vault.wordsWhy: If every device is lost, only these bring your secrets back. still.fail keeps no copy and can't recover them for you
android-settings.vault.wordsOnce: These words are shown only this once
android-settings.vault.noKey: This device has no key to this vault yet
android-settings.vault.noKeyHow: Open Secrets on a device that has the key and give it to this one
android-settings.vault.recoverLead: Enter the 24 words you wrote down, separated by spaces
android-settings.vault.recoveredNone: These words open none of your vaults

android-settings.vault.missing.one: 1 new device has no key yet
android-settings.vault.missing.other: {n} new devices have no key yet

android-settings.vault.giveKey: Give the key to new devices
android-settings.vault.gaveKey: Gave the key to the new devices
android-settings.vault.refusedOld: {name} is too old to hold vaults
android-settings.vault.refusedLock: {name} isn't in security mode and can't hold vaults
android-settings.vault.name: Name
android-settings.vault.agentNote: Each use waits for your approval on your phone
android-settings.vault.howNote: Proxy: the agent gets a placeholder, swapped for the value only on requests to the hosts below. Environment variable: the command sees the value, and the agent might get it
android-settings.vault.sshNote: The key never leaves the station: agents can only sign with it
android-settings.vault.fileTooBig: A file can be at most 64 KB
android-settings.vault.hostsNeeded: A proxy needs the hosts it may go to
android-settings.vault.lastsNote: Approving a request for this secret offers options up to this one. Default uses the default longest approval on the Secrets page, and follows it when that changes.
android-settings.vault.lasts.onceDetail: Every use asks for your approval
android-settings.vault.lasts.hourDetail: Approve up to “this chat, for 1 hour”
android-settings.vault.lasts.chatDetail: Approve up to “this chat, until archived”: it ends when the chat is archived or deleted, 30 days at most
android-settings.vault.lasts.title: Default longest approval
android-settings.vault.lasts.note: When an agent asks for a secret, approval offers options up to the one you choose. Secrets without a setting of their own follow it; edit a secret to give it its own.
android-settings.vault.deleteText: Agents can't ask for it any more, and the value is gone for good
android-settings.vault.approve.onceDetai: For this one command; the next use asks again
android-settings.vault.approve.hourDetai: Used again in this chat for 1 hour without asking
android-settings.vault.approve.chatDetai: Used in this chat until it is archived or deleted, 30 days at most
android-settings.vault.ask.plain: Can read it in plain text
android-settings.vault.save.saveDetail: Each use by an agent still needs your approval
android-settings.vault.save.denyDetail: Don't save it; the agent is notified
android-settings.vault.save.turnOnDetail: Secrets isn't on yet. Turn it on, then come back here to save it
android-settings.vault.request.title: An agent wants “{name}”
android-settings.vault.migrate.body: Secrets saved before security mode was turned on are still stored in plain text on the station
android-settings.profile.pickModels.lead: {name} was added. Only enabled models can be selected for new chats and connects; you can change them later on the profile's page.
android-settings.profile.pickModels.none: This profile lists no models; you can add them later on its page
